title: AI Research Atlas
text:
This atlas is a history of AI safety research from the 1950s to 2026, told alongside reinforcement learning and agents, neural networks and language models, and the institutions that fund, build and govern AI. Each has a lane on the map below.
For most of that time the first three were separate fields. They met between 2017 and 2022, when a reward model trained on people’s comparisons, first tested on Atari games and a simulated robot, became part of the method behind InstructGPT and ChatGPT. Reward hacking, long seen in game-playing agents, and deceptive alignment, until then mostly argued on paper, became things researchers could test on language models.

title: AI Research Atlas
text:
About this atlas
The atlas concentrates on alignment and catastrophic-risk research, and most of its institutional coverage is American and British. Anthropic appears in 16 of the 34 safety entries from 2023 onward, including work with other institutions.
I made the atlas with extensive help from Claude Code and Codex. AI agents drafted most of the cards and checked their dates and sources. I directed the selection and edited the result. Each card lists its sources. Where the main evidence is a developer’s report on its own model, the card says so.
Research snapshot dated 8 November 2026. Page revised 18 November 2026. Corrections and additions are welcome as issues on GitHub.

title: Research
text:
14 Oct 2026


Some Studies of Language Model Weight Edits

The work presented here is my attempt to understand interpretability and model editing methods more deeply. By building on recent advances and trying to find something new, I also learn what others have done before me. For me, the best way to learn is through practice.
Although these studies are written in the form of research papers, I’m not yet confident that I can call them rigorous scientific work. I’m sharing them in the hope that they may be useful to someone besides me.
